description: DC Terminal curated US data center inventory. Public aggregation with per-field confidence and source IDs; not a national census.

facilities.name: xAI Colossus 1
facilities.notes: On-site generation (1,500 MW) is Distilled's figure for mobile gas turbines serving Colossus 1 and 2 combined, not Colossus 1 alone; corroborate with permits/EIA before elevating to confirmed.

facilities.name: Digital Realty IAD39
facilities.notes: Digital Realty Northern Virginia IAD39 in Ashburn (OSM way/701923203). Capacity and opening year are unknown: earlier figures could not be traced to a Digital Realty disclosure and were removed.

facilities.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta — Building 2
facilities.notes: Cooling type reported from public AI campus coverage; water volumes unknown. Microsoft has not disclosed capacity, so per-building MW is unknown (earlier unsourced figures removed). AJC public-records reporting places Fairwater Atlanta within QTS's 615-acre Fayetteville campus; Microsoft and QTS decline to confirm. County-level coordinates.

facilities.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta — Building 4
facilities.notes: Microsoft has not disclosed capacity, so per-building MW is unknown (earlier unsourced figures removed). AJC public-records reporting places Fairwater Atlanta within QTS's 615-acre Fayetteville campus; Microsoft and QTS decline to confirm. County-level coordinates.

facilities.name: IREN Childress
facilities.notes: 750 MW is IREN's stated site power capacity (576 acres, connected directly to ERCOT through IREN-owned on-site substations), not critical IT load. Built for bitcoin mining; IREN is converting part of the site to AI cloud (Horizon 1, 50 MW IT liquid-cooled, delivered to Microsoft). Air and liquid cooling. First-energization year not confirmed in a primary source. City-centroid coordinates.

facilities.name: Riot Platforms Rockdale
facilities.notes: Former Whinstone US facility (construction 2019, operating 2020), acquired by Riot and expanded from 300 MW to 700 MW of developed capacity by end-2022 (Riot 10-K). 700 MW is site power capacity, not critical IT load. Seven buildings; immersion and air cooling; ERCOT grid via Riot-owned substations. City-centroid coordinates.

facilities.name: Google Council Bluffs
facilities.notes: Water figures from public summaries of Google's site-level disclosure (average MGD). Capacity not publicly disclosed. Coordinates from OSM way/578438011 (tagged with Google's Council Bluffs page); OSM also maps more Google buildings ~6 km southeast, not listed separately here.

facilities.name: Meta Hyperion (Richland Parish)
facilities.notes: Meta's largest campus, announced Dec 2024 on the Franklin Farm mega-site (~4M sq ft planned). Recorded at the initial ~2 GW phase expected online by 2030; Meta said in July 2026 it will scale to 5 GW (>$50B), with full build around 2032. GW figures are Meta 'compute capacity' statements, not audited IT load. Power comes through Entergy Louisiana: three new gas plants approved by the LPSC in Aug 2025, plus seven more Meta agreed to fund in March 2026 (10 units, ~7.5 GW in total) that still need LPSC approval. These are utility plants, so BTM stays unknown.

facilities.name: Fermi America — Project Matador
facilities.notes: Fermi's private-grid AI campus ~15 mi NE of Amarillo. TCEQ air permit (NSR 181009 / PSDTX1670 / GHGPSDTX254) authorizes a gas-fired combined-cycle plant that 'will provide electricity to an onsite data center campus'; Fermi says the final permit (Feb 2026) covers 6 GW of a planned 11 GW grid. Data center IT load not disclosed (first lease, TensorWave, Aug 2026: 222 MW of total facility power). Distilled (2026) reported little visible construction, so status stays planned. Coordinates approximate: the US-60 / FM-2373 intersection named in the TCEQ notice.

facilities.name: EdgeCore Mesa campus
facilities.notes: EdgeCore's Mesa campus (May 2025 release): PH01 operating; PH02 and PH03 under construction for 2025-2026 delivery; 206 MW constructed and commissioned since the campus was established in April 2023; designed for 450 MW+ at full build after a 43.87-acre land addition. Recorded MW is the May 2025 commissioned figure, not full build. Salt River Project power; air-cooled closed-loop chilled water design. Coordinates from OSM way/808979618.

facilities.name: Stream Data Centers Phoenix (Goodyear) campus
facilities.notes: Stream's Goodyear campus west of Phoenix. Phoenix I opened in 2020 as the first of five planned buildings on 157 acres, with up to 200 MW of critical load at full build per Stream's launch materials. Delivered MW not disclosed, so capacity is unknown. Coordinates from OSM ('Stream Data Centers PHX-1', way/468707940).

facilities.name: Hut 8 King Mountain (McCamey)
facilities.notes: Built by Compute North as a 280 MW hosting site co-located with the King Mountain Wind Farm (278.2 MW) and energized Aug 2022, billed as a behind-the-meter wind project; now held by the King Mountain JV (Hut 8 ~50%, a Fortune 200 renewable producer ~50%). 280 MW is site power capacity. GEM notes the wind farm's output is fully contracted to three utilities and assumes most power is grid-supplied via a nearby substation, so BTM is 'reported' and on-site MW is left unknown. Coordinates from GEM.

facilities.name: Equinix DC12 (Ashburn)
facilities.notes: IBX on Equinix's Ashburn campus, opened Oct 2017 ($98.5M; phase 1 added 1,500 cabinets / 57,800 gross sq ft, ~3,000 cabinets at full build). Equinix states indirect evaporative cooling (IDEC) and a LEED Gold design. Equinix does not publish site MW or site-level water, so those stay unknown (earlier illustrative water values removed). Coordinates from OSM way/596690175.

facilities.name: Project Jupiter (Stargate New Mexico)
facilities.notes: Stargate site in Santa Teresa, Doña Ana County: ~1,400 acres, four data centers planned for Oracle (18-year lease) with OpenAI as the primary user; the county approved up to $165B in industrial revenue bonds in Sept 2025. Under construction since late 2025; Oracle targets power-up by end of 2026. Power is planned from an on-site microgrid (switched from gas turbines to natural-gas fuel cells): 2,450 MW per Distilled, ~2.5 GW per NPR. Yucca Growth Infrastructure's air permit applications (up to ~2,880 MW) were stayed by the NM Supreme Court (Sept 2026) and the State Land Office denied the gas pipeline right-of-way, so the timeline is at risk. IT load not disclosed. Oracle cites ~11 million gallons of recycled non-potable water but no daily rate, so water stays unknown. City-centroid coordinates (site lies SE of NM-136 / NM-9, ~2 mi north of the border).

facilities.name: Vantage Quincy (WA1) campus
facilities.notes: Three-building campus (WA11-WA13) on 68 acres, ~775k sq ft; WA13 (64 MW) was delivered Oct 2023, completing 89 MW of IT capacity. Powered by Grant County PUD (hydro-heavy mix). Vantage describes a closed-loop, air-cooled chiller system. Water volumes not disclosed. Coordinates from OSM (WA11 building, way/337127817).

facilities.name: Google The Dalles
facilities.notes: Google's first company-built campus (2006). Water figures are 2024 calendar-year city/utility records released after The Oregonian public-records case: 461.1M gal withdrawn, 361.4M gal consumed. Capacity not publicly disclosed.

facilities.name: Switch Citadel Campus (Tahoe Reno)
facilities.notes: TR1 marketed at up to 130 MW; full campus planned at 650 MW / 7.2M sq ft (corporate 'up to' figures, treated as reported). Five TR buildings mapped in OSM; row is campus-level.

facilities.name: Meta Prineville
facilities.notes: Meta's first owned campus (2011). Meta publishes fleet-wide WUE (~0.18–0.26 L/kWh) but not audited per-facility water for Prineville, so water stays unknown here. Capacity not disclosed.

facilities.name: Meta Los Lunas
facilities.notes: Served by dedicated NMRD solar plants (incl. 'NMRD Data Center III', 50 MW) via utility PPA — separate EIA plant records, so power is grid-supplied, not behind-the-meter.

facilities.name: Microsoft San Antonio campus
facilities.notes: Multi-building Westover Hills campus; Microsoft confirms operating datacenters in Bexar and Medina counties. Campus capacity not publicly disclosed.

facilities.name: Apple Mesa (Global Data & Command Center)
facilities.notes: 1.3M sq ft former GT Advanced facility, $2B conversion announced 2015, opened 2017. Associated 70 MW solar is off-site via SRP PPA, so not BTM; on-site generation unknown.

facilities.name: 350 E Cermak (Lakeside Technology Center)
facilities.notes: 1.1M sq ft carrier hotel on Chicago's Near South Side; press-reported 109 MW is total facility power capacity, not IT load — recorded as reported with that caveat.

facilities.name: Meta Gallatin
facilities.notes: Operating Sumner County campus; capacity and water not publicly disclosed at facility level.

facilities.name: Microsoft Licking County campuses (cancelled)
facilities.notes: $1B three-site plan announced Oct 2024, cancelled April 2025. Microsoft retains the land, so future development is possible; row records the cancelled projects. County-centroid coordinates.

facilities.name: Greenidge Generation (Dresden)
aliases: Greenidge Power Plant and Data Center
facilities.notes: Bitcoin mining co-located inside a 106 MW gas plant the operator owns — textbook behind-the-meter, documented in SEC filings and NY Title V permit. Mining load has ranged ~14–85 MW; excess power sold to NYISO (hybrid). IT load left unknown because the split shifts dynamically.

facilities.name: Stargate Abilene (Crusoe campus)
facilities.notes: Flagship Stargate site; roughly half the buildings already operating, so status=under_construction understates partial operation. 1,200 MW is the press-reported full-buildout figure, not current load (~300 MW). Permit authorizes ~360 MW of behind-the-meter simple-cycle gas explicitly for on-site data center use; grid supply (incl. wind) also used.

facilities.name: Galaxy Helios (Dickens County)
facilities.notes: Built 2022 as Argo Blockchain's Helios bitcoin mine (~180 MW); acquired by Galaxy Digital and converted to an AI campus hosting CoreWeave under a 15-year lease. Phase I complete July 2026: 200 MW gross / 133 MW critical IT load, rent commenced Q2 2026. ERCOT-approved campus capacity 1.63 GW (potential 3.6 GW); Phase II (260 MW IT) targeted H1 2027 — only delivered Phase I load is recorded here. Grid-supplied via ERCOT; no public evidence of on-site generation.
